page0.text:
"Oof..."
I'm overwhelmed by the crowd the moment we get off the bus.
It's lively in front of the train station.
It's a nice weekend morning before 10 AM, so it would be weird for it to not be lively.

page1.text:
"...I am surprised. There're this many people that gather when it's a weekend."
Saber looks at the town, bewildered.
She has never seen the town during the day, so her reaction is only natural.

page2.text:
"..."
As I say this, I'm also stunned by the crowd.
"Well, where should we go? Do you two have any requests?"
However...
Unlike us, Tohsaka is full of energy.

page3.text:
"Uh... That's troubling. I don't know any fun places."
"I thought so. What about you, Saber? Do you have anywhere you want to go?"

page4.text:
"Me...? No, I do not have any place that I am particularly interested in. First of all, I am Shirou's guardian.
If this is you and Shirou's day off, please consider me not here."

page5.text:
"Wha—"
"Really? Then we can go where I want to go?
Ohh. If you two don't have any input, does that mean you guys will give me absolute obedience to my plan?"

page6.text:
"Whaaa—"
I feel a chill run up my spine.
Tohsaka smirks at us with a scary stare.

page7.text:
"H-Hold on, don't say it in a scary way!
First of all, I said I would keep you company, but I never said I was going on a d-date with you. This is just for the three of us to hang out."

page8.text:
"Too bad, that's what society calls a date.
Come on, give it up already. Girls will hate you if you don't know when to give up."

page9.text:
"H-Hate me? Like who?"
"Who could it be? Well, I guess being stubborn may be a good trait. Right, Saber?"

page10.text:
"Yes. Shirou is a sore loser. His persistent mind is reassuring during battle."
"See. Aren't you glad, Shirou?"

page11.text:
"Ugh..."
Tohsaka smiles.
Geez, what's so fun about making fun of other people!?

page12.text: "Well, why don't we go to Verde first? You two haven't eaten breakfast yet, right? We can go window-shopping after a quick cup of tea to warm ourselves up."

page13.text:
Tohsaka starts walking.
I think Verde is the name of the new department store that they recently made?

page14.text: "Hey, I'm gonna leave you behind if you're slow. Breakfast is only till 10 AM, so we have to hurry before it ends."

page15.text:
"Wai..."
She won't stop, even if I call for her.
It seems like Tohsaka has no time to waste and won't give me the time to settle down.

page16.text:
"Shirou. Rin is walking away."
Ugh... Geez, fine! I'll go anywhere you want!
I slap myself on both cheeks and get pumped up.

page17.text:
"Come on, Saber! Don't get lost!"
"Yes. Please do not lose sight of Rin either, Shirou."

page18.text:
We both start running.
In the crowded town, Tohsaka doesn't look back.
It seems like she's absolutely certain that we're going to follow her.

page19.text:
And...
Before I realize it, I've fallen into a more helpless situation.

page20.text:
"This store's atmosphere is completely different from the first one.
Rin, why are we here?"
"It's just a little break. I thought you both may be tired. If we don't take a break now, it looks like your springs will wear out."
"Oh? It certainly was a hectic two hours, but not enough exercise to have to take a break..."

page21.text:
"Maybe for you, Saber. But, there are things that wear down in places you can't see.
What seems like a normal floor to us can be a poisonous swamp to others."

page22.text:
"Oh, I'm having this banana parfait. You should have this devil's sundae, Saber.
What about you, Emiya? Do you eat sweets?"

page23.text:
"Who'd eat that first thing in the morning? I'll have this coffee blend."
"Oh my, such a boy. But are you sure? You'll be in trouble if you don't replenish your HP."
"..."
It goes without saying, but eating ice cream together here would be a whole other dimension, and I have no appetite to begin with.
Also, she's not good with technology, yet she knows something like that?

page24.text:
"So stubborn. Well, that's fun in its own way, so it's fine."
I don't know what's so fun, but the red devil is smirking. You should be the one eating the devil's sundae.
"Shirou, sugar intake is not to be taken lightly. If you are exhausted as Rin says, what about this 'mango rush & cream'?"
Saber subtly offers me the menu.

page25.text:
"...Yes. I cannot say this too loudly, but I would hide from the others to eat sweet fruits when we traveled for days in the military. Chocolate and the like are said to have originated from alchemy as well."
"I've never heard that before.
...So. Saber, you want to try the mango rush, too?"
"Yes. I would appreciate if I can get a bite."

page26.text:
"..."
...How lonely.
Saber has left my nervous self and has already fallen under Tohsaka's evil influence.

page27.text:
"Oh, there's no need to hold back, Saber. We should go ahead and order both."
"Hm... As much as I would like to, that would be an unnecessary order. It is a different story if I were hungry, but I cannot possibly order excess food simply out of interest..."

page28.text:
"That responsibility is the best part of dates.
In this situation, the way it works is that Emiya treats us with a smile and we experience his generosity."
"I see, how wonderful. I am always in awe of your direction, Rin."

page29.text:
"..."
This is beyond evil influence.
Saber was already an enemy on Tohsaka's side.

page30.text:
"Well then, time to go over the order.
Banana parfait, devil's sundae, mango rush, and a coffee blend. Will that be all, sir?"
"...Why are you asking me? That's fine, do what you want. It's not like I have the right to veto, right?
And if you ask me, the orange sponge cake would be better than the mango rush."
That would probably suit Tohsaka and Saber's tastes better.

page31.text:
"Then I'll take your advice.
Don't lose that part of you, Emiya."
So began the least relaxing break imaginable.

page32.text:
...Right. To be honest, I think I was nothing but nervous the first hour.
Even by herself, Tohsaka stands out.
Her eye-catching, vivid red clothes and long silky black hair.
The colors alone stand out, but Tohsaka herself is a flawless beauty.
With Saber by her side, it goes without saying that they make a striking pair.

page33.text:
"Hm? What are you looking at?
Oh, did you calm your nerves down?"
"...Humph. Well, after being dragged around this much, then yeah."
...Damn it. I really hate to admit it, but Tohsaka's suggestion to take a break was detestably correct.

page34.text: "Okay. Then, that means I can raise the bar a bit more, right?"

page35.text:
The strongest enemy smirks.
Honestly, I can't even understand myself.
I can fight back-to-back with her as a Master, but right now, even the gestures that I've gotten used to seeing makes my heart skip a beat.
...It must be because I rashly got too close to her, so it's hard to interact with her normally now.

page36.text:
"Oh, yeah. Since we have the opportunity, let's do that next.
Saber, are you interested in accessories?"
"Ornaments, you say?
I do not collect them, but neither am I uninterested in looking at them."
"Then let's go to a store like that next. I want to make you try on a lot of things."

page37.text:
...
My nerves don't calm down. Her bright smile alone makes me dazzled.
An unknown panic or agitation makes my chest hurt a bit.
That was why I thought that we should hurry back home and devise a strategy, instead of going on a date.

page38.text:
But...
Um, what kind of magecraft was cast to make it turn out this way?

page39.text: "Man, that was so funny. That was the funniest thing I've seen in a while."

page40.text: "Is that so? I cannot tell. Shirou did not look like himself earlier."

page41.text:
"That's what's good. I didn't think he would look so much like a spoiled rich kid just by putting glasses on. You should've bought those glasses, Shirou."
Tohsaka must've loved it, as she's still laughing.

page42.text:
...It all happened about ten minutes ago.
I don't know what Tohsaka was thinking, but she took us to the glasses shop and played around by putting fake glasses on Saber.

page43.text:
I became a victim of circumstance as well, and one of the glasses she put on me became a hit for her.
It was a pair of fake glasses with a thick frame and formal design.

page44.text: ...Ugh, no thanks. Look, I'm never wearing fake glasses. I already have a babyface, so I can't afford to look even more like a kid.

page45.text: "Huh? Oh, I see, you were aware of it. But I don't think you need to worry. There's nothing wrong with the way you are now."

page46.text:
"Stu—There's a problem with the way I am now! My face can't be helped, but I need a bit more height!"
"Oh? I think your height is average."
"It's not. I'll be able to brace myself if I'm taller. I need at least Issei's height."

page47.text:
"I said you don't have to worry. You'll still grow more."
"...I'm glad to hear that, but what's your reasoning behind that?"

page48.text:
"Huh... Oh, yeah. You're well-built, so you'll grow if you get your nutrition, right? I thought you'd grow if you use photosynthesis."
"What kind of leaf are you talking about? Don't treat me like some flower."

page49.text:
"Oh. Emiya, are you mad...?"
"Nah. I'll take it with a grain of salt... Well, it seems like I can look forward to it if you say so."

page50.text:
"...Yes. I can't make any promises about your height, but I'm sure you'll become a fine man. That I can guarantee for sure, Shirou."
"Wha—"
W-Why would you say things that make my face boil!?

page51.text:
"Hah, you're blushing. I like you since your emotions always show on your face."
"Ugh..."
S-She's playing around with me.
She's definitely playing around with me.

page52.text: "Guh, you evil woman! Is it fun for you to tease a guy your age!?"

page53.text:
"Of course. It depends on the person, but your reactions are the best."
...Dear God.
Please give her divine punishment.
Not for my sake, but for the sake of all the guys at my school.

page54.text:
"Oh, let's stop playing around with Shirou and get to the main part. Do you want to let out some stress before lunch?"
Tohsaka puts her fists together and swings them.

page55.text:
"...Could it be...?"
It's obvious from her gesture.
Well, but is it possible for a girl to suggest it as part of the date course...?

page56.text:
"What else could there be other than a batting cage, Shirou? Don't tell me you don't know it."
Tohsaka, the (former) school idol, asks me if I'm serious.

page57.text:
"Of course I know!
What I want to say is that batting cages aren't for girls..."
Saying that, I imagine Tohsaka standing in the batter's box.

page58.text:
"..."
...Crap. It does look strange, but why does she look so reliable?

page59.text: "What, then do you want to go to the aquarium instead? I think they had the penguin army vs. a giant seal from the North Sea, the flaming freezing three-game match, but it's a third-rate attraction."

page60.text:
...
Well, I think it's a second-rate attraction, but I don't know about going to an aquarium when it's such a nice day outside.

page61.text:
"Rin. What is a batting cage?"
"Huh? Oh, well it's something you would be good at. You can say that it's a well-rounded physical exercise considered to be special training in some cases."
Woah.
Tohsaka's putting it in a ridiculous way.

page62.text:
"...Hm. I cannot ignore that."
"Yeah, you should try it since it feels good. I bet you'll be able to win all the prizes."
Tohsaka raises Saber's expectations irresponsibly and starts walking again.

page63.text:
"...Ugh."
I watch her back and start running, having no other choice.
There's no point arguing against Tohsaka's energy.
I can't stop her, and it doesn't feel too bad being dragged around like this.

page64.text:
So that's what it means.
My nerves calm down since I'm having fun.
I was taken around so much that I didn't have time to rest, and the nervousness went away.
Tohsaka urges me to go to the next place, and I respond reluctantly, while Saber watches over us quietly.

page65.text:
...That was really fun.
The town I only used to walk by...
I didn't know that all the things I didn't involve myself in were so meaningful.

page66.text:
...
As soon as I think so, something like a cage falls on me, and it makes sense.
You don't deserve this.
You're unworthy of this.
Somewhere deep down, I tell myself.

page67.text:
I-I'm tired.
I never expected that I would be at bat five times for thirty pitches each, for a total of 150 swings.
It's all because...

page68.text:
"W-What is it, Shirou? It is troubling if you look at me like that."
It's because she's a sore loser.

page69.text:
"That was a miscalculation... I didn't think that Saber would be so competitive."
Tohsaka sighs next to me.
She also...

page70.text:
"Oh, I'll only play one game. My hands will get rough if I grip the bat that much."
...Said something like that, but ended up playing another game with Saber, then complained afterwards about how her shoulders were tired and her hands hurt.

page71.text:
What are you saying? You only played twice and just held onto the bat in the back after that. I did it five times. Five times! And at the fastest speed too!
...Man, Saber would get mad if I take it too easy on her but would sulk if I beat her too bad. It was a hell of an hour."

page72.text: "I-I did not sulk! I was only filled with spirit. First of all, this is nothing compared to our matches in the dojo. It is your fault for getting tired."

page73.text:
"...I get it. Saber's the type to get mad when she loses in games, huh?"
I sigh and wobble forward.

page74.text:
Here's what I found out today. First, don't bet with Saber.
Second, a rule where the one who achieves ten more hits than their opponent wins becomes an eternal hell if the abilities of those playing are equal.
Third, Saber is weaker than us if she limits her magical energy.

page75.text:
...Or rather, is Tohsaka the abnormal one for hitting 120 kmph balls like it's nothing?
It's natural since Saber is the smallest out of all of us, so it goes without saying that Tohsaka is strong for a girl.

page76.text:
"How rude. Batting doesn't equal arm strength.
Even a girl can hit if the swing speed and the angles are right."

page77.text:
"Well, that's for one or two pitches. Usually their arm cramps up. Aren't you doing push-ups before you go to bed? That's the only thing I can think of."
I say sarcastically, as if to get back at her.
However...

page78.text:
"...I-I do. Is there a problem?"
"...Uh, no... Nice."
Sometimes she makes these counterattacks, so I wasn't able to make a comeback at all.

page79.text:
"A-Anyway, let's have lunch. It's already past 2 PM. I need to eat something, since I'm getting dizzy."
A family restaurant along the bridge should be the most convenient around here.
There's a lot on the menu, so Saber shouldn't have any complaints either.

page80.text:
"Is that fine with you, Tohsaka? It's not like you have any place in mind, right?"
I call to Tohsaka.

page81.text:
"I-I do. It's not like it has to be there, but I have it planned out."
"Oh, okay. So, where is it?"

page82.text:
"...Here."
"Huh? What do you mean 'here'?"
"I mean here. It's a nice day out, so we're going to have a picnic at the park."

page83.text:
...I look around.
I don't see any food place or even a hotdog stand.

page84.text:
"Tohsaka, don't tell me you're planning to get delivery."
"...Hey now. What do you think that tote bag you've been carrying this whole time is?"
"Huh...?"

page85.text:
Oh.
Come to think of it, she did give me this bag to carry this morning.

page86.text:
"...Hm. It smells like mustard. So this is..."
"Lunch, of course. Didn't I mention that I prepared that much?"

page87.text:
She glares at me in objection.
...Come to think of it, she did say something like that.

page88.text: "Wow, I'm surprised. I didn't think this would be that well thought-through."

page89.text: "Of course it is. I invited you, so I prepared accordingly."

page90.text:
"Yeah, the mystery's also solved now. You used the bread for this, huh?
Man, I totally thought you got hungry in the middle of the night and ate it. It seems absurd to eat a whole loaf, but I thought it might be possible in your case."

page91.text:
I see, I see.
I nod twice, thinking that I got a huge load off my chest.
"Oh."
When I look up, Tohsaka was making a scary face.

page93.text:
"Can you stop talking and start preparing lunch? All the utensils are inside the tote bag. Also, I'm going to kill you if you're too slow."
"Oh... Yes. I will do my best."

page94.text:
I secure our spot on the grass.
Man, that was scary.
It's bad for my heart for her to say a joke that doesn't sound like a joke with that big smile...

page95.text:
And...
Lunch starts two hours late, but...

page96.text:
"Huh? What happened, Shirou? Why are you spacing out?
...Oh, are you not good with spicy food?"

page97.text:
Right next to me...
Tohsaka, who's sitting in a position close enough to touch her if I reach out, says.

page98.text:
"Huh? Oh, no, I'm fine. It's an intense flavor, but this is good."
I say my honest opinion and take another bite.

page99.text:
"Really? That's good. It's a talent to be able to make a sandwich that tastes bad, right? I thought for a second that I had that useless talent."
Tohsaka laughs delightfully.

page100.text:
...
If I looked like I was spacing out, it was probably because she was dazzling.

page101.text:
We eat lunch on the grass under the clear blue sky.
Even that by itself is peaceful enough, but having Tohsaka there is more than I can handle and my nerves from this morning return.

page102.text:
"Oh. You have a piece of tomato on your lip. Do you want me to get it for you?"
"Bu...! W-W-W-W-W-What are you saying all of a sudden!? I can get that myself!"
I wipe my mouth with my sleeve.

page103.text:
"Oh."
Shoot.
I got an unlucky red stain on my clothes now.

page104.text: "Oops, I guess I played around too much. I'm sorry, it was too funny since you react exactly how I expect you to."

page105.text: I don't know if she's apologizing or suppressing her laughter, but she hands me a napkin while she holds her stomach.

page106.text:
"...Humph. Whatever, I've been like this the whole day anyway. I don't care."
I accept the napkin and wipe my sleeve.
The red stain doesn't come off.
...Hm. Tohsaka must've used an original sauce.
The stain is quite stubborn and doesn't easily come off.

page107.text: "But just you watch. I'll learn from today's lesson and won't budge from anything starting tomorrow. Don't think it'll go your way forever."

page108.text:
"Oh. So that means I don't have to hold back starting tomorrow, huh?
That's good, I was getting tired of putting up a façade."
The red devil replies calmly.

page109.text: "...Oh, no, I take that back. It'll take some time, so I'd appreciate it if you can keep it at that level."

page110.text: "Really? If you say so, but let me know if you want to level up. I'll knock you out without reserve."

page111.text:
"...Damn. I'll get you someday."
I'm not bitter that I lost, but I complain like I am.
...It's somehow really vexing, so I take it out on the sandwich in front of me.

page112.text:
I eat up the sandwiches.
I was hungry and it's Tohsaka's handmade meal, so I'm going to eat it all by myself.
...Well, Saber already consumed a third of the sandwiches.

page113.text:
So Saber and I eat the sandwiches.
Tohsaka must be full, as she watches us.

page114.text: "Your body seems to be doing well. It looks like I can pull you around without holding back in the afternoon."

page115.text:
She makes an evil smile again.
That's more like...
She's looking forward to seeing me worn out from being dragged around than the actual activities itself.

page116.text: "Humph, don't take me too lightly. I won't complain just from being pulled around. Yesterday aside, I've been doing well today."

page117.text:
"I see. Then I guess you're all right."
Tohsaka sighs with relief and reaches for a sandwich.
It's as if the weight is off her shoulders.

page118.text:
"...?"
The moment I tilt my head, wondering why she would say that...
"Oh."
Everything fits together.

page119.text:
...
Come to think of it, it was really unnatural.
The reason Tohsaka came to my place.
Archer knew what was wrong with my body.
He must've heard that I Projected his swords and knew there was something wrong with my body.

page120.text:
That's fine.
But Archer, who wasn't there at the time, knew about the Projection because Tohsaka told him.
Then...
Just like Tohsaka told Archer about our battle with Caster, didn't Archer tell Tohsaka about the penalty on my body...?

page121.text:
"Tohsaka."
"Huh? What?"
"Why did you come to my place yesterday? It's strange for you to stay over too. I didn't notice all this yesterday because Fuji-nee stirred things up."

page122.text:
...
A brief moment.
But I hear Tohsaka gasp.

page123.text:
"I don't particularly have a reason. I just felt like it yesterday. I thought it might be fun once in a while."
"I see. It certainly was lively and fun yesterday."
"Right?"
"Yeah. But thank you."

page124.text:
"...!"
Wow.
She turned red in an instant.

page125.text:
"W-W-W-What are you misunderstanding....!? I-I wasn't concerned about you...!"
"I know, it's not good to have your ally die. That's why you came to check up on me, right?"

page126.text:
"Uh... T-That's right. You're pretty smart."
"Yeah. But I still appreciate it.
I don't know what you were planning, but I know you cared for me."

page127.text:
"..."
She groans in dissatisfaction, with her face still red.
That gesture is so cute it makes me smile.

page128.text:
"...I see, I get it."
I guess I get it.
It might be a different kind, but making the person you like embarrassed makes me really happy.

page129.text:
The weather changes once we finish lunch.
The sky that was clear is now clouded and it looks like it could rain at any moment.
